argument:
Sime's declining borrowings and cash-covered ordinary dividends provide meaningful value compensation at 9.58x earnings. Nevertheless reported profit fell 14.5%, and after ordinary, NCI and sukuk distributions only about RM53m remained from the specified cash surplus. This leaves much less discretionary headroom than ordinary-dividend coverage alone implies.

Management-defined core profit growth of 32.6% is distinct from IFRS earnings and includes a reconciliation that deserves scrutiny alongside Motors impairments and restructuring. FY27 only promises broadly consistent core performance, not another growth surge. The bull's income case is defensible, but cyclical deterioration or additional investment can strain thin all-distribution coverage. Debt reduction mitigates risk; a 5.62% reported yield does not guarantee that future distributions and price appreciation both persist.
key_points: All stated distributions leave thin cash headroom.
Reported profit declined despite management-defined core growth.
Cyclicality and restructuring qualify yield durability.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull's ordinary-dividend coverage is genuine, but NCI and sukuk payouts leave only about RM53m headroom. Core growth cannot be extrapolated when FY27 guidance is merely broadly consistent and reported earnings declined.
